verdict: MATERIAL DEFECT CONFIRMED — the completed-pass counter increments BEFORE post-operation constraints are evaluated

experiment.construction: a METADATA_ONLY plan with a caller-bound AccountConstraint(metadata_reads, FLOOR, 999) that the run cannot satisfy; RoutePassSpec(expected=1, maximum=1)
experiment.result: the source operation RETURNED, the postcondition FAILED (POST_EXECUTION_CONSTRAINT_FAILED), and _passes_completed was left at 1

governing_question: may full_route_passes_observed truthfully increment before the postcondition is satisfied?
determination: NO. A completed governed route pass means the WHOLE bound execution succeeded, including its required post-operation EXACT/FLOOR constraints. Counting the pass on mere operation-return makes the counter an 'operation returned' counter wearing the name of a completed governed pass — the exact conflation the accounting law forbids elsewhere (a lower-layer account may not stand in for the outer one).

why_the_current_comment_is_insufficient.candidate_comment: 'A pass counts ONLY on success. A failed attempt leaves the count at 0, so a failed first attempt can never be reported as a completed pass.'
why_the_current_comment_is_insufficient.gap: that is true only for failures that raise BEFORE the increment (i.e. inside session.run). A failure that raises AFTER it (any post-operation constraint breach, including the outer EXACT check itself) leaves the count incremented.

self_defeating_detail.observation: when the outer EXACT expectation itself fails, the code raises POST_EXECUTION_CONSTRAINT_FAILED, but _passes_completed has already been incremented — so the very check that detects the failure runs after the count has recorded success
self_defeating_detail.consequence: a subsequent execute() is then refused, so the bound execution can neither truthfully report 0 completed passes nor complete the required pass

required_completion_rule.rule: a governed full route pass is COMPLETED only when the bound execution as a whole succeeds: the source operation returned AND every caller-bound post-operation EXACT/FLOOR/MAXIMUM constraint holds AND the outer route-pass expectation holds
required_completion_rule.implementation_requirement: perform all post-operation checks FIRST and only then increment the completed-pass counter (or increment provisionally and roll back on any post-operation failure)
required_completion_rule.preserve: the distinction between operation-return success and completed-pass success must be visible in the receipt, not only in control flow
